demographics.income: USD 60k–110k blended (contract work + a small product doing ~USD 3k MRR)
demographics.occupation: Solo technical founder of a niche B2B SaaS, plus one side venture

psychographics.identity: A builder who wants to be a steward — sees the business as a long game, not a lottery ticket
psychographics.lifestyle: Works in bursts; travels 6–8 weeks a year; has already had one burnout that stalled the product for a quarter
psychographics.aspirations: A calm, durable business that keeps compounding when she is offline, and room to start a second venture without abandoning the first
psychographics.community: Indie Hackers, a founder Discord, X build-in-public circles, a local coworking guild

challenges.challenge: The company stops when she stops
challenges.current_solution: Zapier chains, scheduled posts, a VA 5 hours a week
challenges.why_it_fails: Automations run blind — nothing notices when the business drifts off-mission or runway shrinks
challenges.quote: Every time I take a week off, the queue backs up and I come back to a smaller business.

challenges.current_solution: Tried an 'AI runs your company' tool for a month
challenges.why_it_fails: It reported tasks complete that never shipped and emailed prospects the wrong price
challenges.quote: I don't need more autonomy. I need to know when it's wrong.

challenges.current_solution: Agent posting 20 times a day on X
challenges.why_it_fails: Optimizes activity, not viability — five weeks, net zero growth, real credits burned
challenges.quote: It was very busy doing nothing.

challenges.current_solution: A Notion brand doc nobody reads, including the agents
challenges.why_it_fails: The brand is write-once; nothing feeds learnings back into it
challenges.quote: The product I'm selling today isn't the one my landing page describes.

positive: relief that the business is still alive tomorrow
pride in a coherent, honest brand
trust earned from a legible record
freedom to rest or start something new
negative: dread of coming back to a dead business
shame of an agent misrepresenting her to customers
anxiety about runway she can't see
exhaustion from being the only heartbeat

salience.problem_solved: Keeping a small business alive, on-mission and advancing when the founder isn't driving
salience.one_sentence: Cambium is the patient operator above your AI agents that keeps your business in the game.

points_of_difference: Viability bounds (solvency, mission coherence, legal/ethical) instead of throughput targets
Fail-closed gate on every irreversible or paid move
Setpoint moves only on real customer evidence, capped per wake
Replayable decision log with honest status labels
points_of_parity: Orchestrates agents for build, marketing and operations
Affordable for a solo founder (Genesis free)
core_features: Founder and ICP NPC simulations (propose, never commit)

usage_locations: laptop at a café between trips
phone via Telegram mini-app while travelling

positive: It tells me when it's unsure
concerns: Will the math language be over my head?
judgments.credibility: Shows its work: labelled claims, replay log, fail-closed defaults, and a free Genesis tier to try before trusting

feelings.tone: Honest and unhurried; names uncertainty; never hypes or pressures

resonance.why_missed: Every competitor sells how much the agent does; none sell what it keeps alive
resonance.mission_alignment: She wants a business she can tend for years, not a launch that burns out
resonance.why_choose_us: The only operator built for the infinite game: it protects margin to survival first and treats revenue as a regulated output, so she can step away without dread

secondary_persona.summary: Runs a 6-person micro-studio with 9 live client and owned brands; each drifts off-voice once the launch team moves on; wants one operator across many gardens with per-brand memory and a portfolio viability view.
